analysis: The code snippet calls String.substring(int) only when at >= 0, where at is obtained from sender.indexOf('@'). The indexOf method returns -1 if '@' is not present, otherwise a value between 0 and sender.length()-1 inclusive. When at >= 0, it is guaranteed to be a valid beginIndex (non-negative and less than the string length), so the condition for IndexOutOfBoundsException is not met. The surrounding checks (sender not null, from not null/empty) further ensure the string is non-null and has content. Therefore, the only declared exception (IndexOutOfBoundsException) is avoided.
answer: IndexOutOfBoundsException: throwing condition is avoided because beginIndex is always in the valid range [0, sender.length()-1] when substring is called.
remark: All declared exceptions are fully avoided. The only potential exception, IndexOutOfBoundsException, cannot occur because the beginIndex used (the index of '@') is always within the bounds of the string when the substring call is executed.
